Rae (PM): Heads-up: Draft PRD for fallback compatibility + tiered routing ready for review. Need acceptance criteria and launch asks by EOD Fri. Key customer asks: region-aware fallbacks, model-variant compatibility (quantized + fp), and per-tenant strict isolation. Link: https://redwood.internal/prd/fallback-compat :eyes:
Samir (Eng): Can you paste the high-level acceptance criteria here? hard to click during standup
Rae (PM): Acceptance criteria: - deterministic fallback decision tree and reproducible logs - perf: p95 latency <= 120ms for Tier-A routes under normal load - compatibility matrix populated for top 8 models/variants - rollout: canary @1% with automated rollback on error rate > 2x baseline - audit: per-request variant id + reason persisted for 90d
Jordan (Infra): Add SLA test for burst scenarios (10x baseline qps for 30s). Also need explicit region routing tests: EU->US fallback must respect data residency flag (no content crossing when disallowed).
Maya (ML): Model compatibility notes: quantized variants sometimes change tokenization/contrasting logits. Recommend adding a tokenization smoke test + quality delta threshold: perplexity/LL delta <= 2% vs baseline for core prompts. Also check tool-calling + structured output features when applicable.
Luis (Eng-Platform): Ops constraints: dedicated pools can't host >2 incompatible quant profiles per node without big perf hit. We should gate fallback policy so it won't mix incompatible quant types on same node. Also add alerting for fallback-induced cost delta (>15% monthly).
Ivy (Support): From support intake: two enterprise customers asked for deterministic model-variant affinity for auditability. They want per-request logs that show chosen variant id and the fallback reason (capacity/feature/cost).
Samir (Eng): Edge case: variant exists in region but lacks required feature (e.g., function-calling). Fallback must run feature compatibility checks before considering a variant. If no feature-compatible variant, return graceful degraded response + clear client error.
Rae (PM): Agreed. Proposed: feature_compat check first, then latency, then region affinity, then cost. Launch gates: security review complete, load tests pass (including bursts), 2 customer pilots signed, docs + FAQ, and audit retention validated.
Jordan (Infra): Also add a forced-rollback window param (e.g., 30m) and a circuit-breaker when fallback rate crosses threshold. Otherwise we risk cascading fallthroughs.
Jordan (Infra): Quick config sketch for the PRD (ops-friendly):
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  tiers: [A, B, C]
  checks_order: [feature_compat, latency, region, cost]
  canary: 0.01
  rollback_window_minutes: 30
  audit_retention_days: 90
```
routing-bot: policy-lint report: 3 warnings - missing rollback_window, missing audit_retention, no canary threshold for tier-B
Rae (PM): Thanks, I'll fold these into the PRD. Who can own the rollout plan & SLO tests? @Luis?
Luis (Eng-Platform): I'll own rollout + SLO test harness. Will put together Jenkins job + perf dashboard. Sync tomorrow 10am.
Maya (ML): I'll add the eval harness changes and the tokenization smoke tests to the ml-evals repo.
Samir (Eng): I'll draft an RFC for the compatibility matrix schema (fields: model, variant_id, quant_profile, region_availability, features, quality_metrics).
Ivy (Support): I'll prepare a customer-facing FAQ that explains deterministic affinity and what logs we provide.
Rae (PM): Great. Action items: Samir RFC, Luis rollout plan, Maya evals, Jordan infra tests. I'll update PRD and ping for final review before EOD Fri. :thumbsup:
